newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 5.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 5. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

Indonesian Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo has rejected calls for third-party mediation in its dispute over its Timor national car which Japan, Europe and the United States have taken to the World Trade Organisation.

Former Interior Minister and retired general Rudini has said the armed forces should give up all its 75 seats in the parliament that it currently holds as it was not consistent with the nation's constitution.

The initial public offering of Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) 1946 which opened on Monday was met with enthusiasm at sales points in Jakarta, Bandung and Surabaya. The state-owned bank is offering 25 percent of its capital in the sell-off.

Three firms have announced they hold a controlling interest in Indonesia's largest automobile manufacturer PT Astra Internasional. The consortium includes "Bob" Hasan's Nusamba group, bank PT Danamon International and PT Indo Artsa Boga, a subsidary of flour producers PT Bogasari.
Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said that he hoped Indonesia would reach the status of newly industrialised nation by the year 2018.
Douglas Warner, head of JP Morgan, thanked President Suharto for choosing his firm as financial advisors in the BNI float.
